articles.title_orig: As War Roils Energy Markets, China Sees Its Emissions Drop
articles.title_zh: As War Roils Energy Markets, China Sees Its Emissions Drop
articles.content_orig:
Rooftop solar in Chengdu, China. Pexels
China’s carbon dioxide emissions have been flat or falling for more than two years as renewables stunt demand for fossil fuels. But the country just saw its steepest quarterly drop since the Covid pandemic, thanks to energy shocks rippling from the Iran war.
Between July and September, China saw its carbon dioxide emissions fall by 3.1 percent, according to an analysis of official figures and commercial data by Carbon Brief . That is the biggest quarterly decline since the 2022 pandemic lockdowns.
The analysis finds oil use fell by 4 percent, year on year, as Chinese drivers flocked to electric vehicles at a time when the Iran war is driving up the cost of fuel. Electric cars accounted for two in three new passenger vehicles sold in China in September, according to industry data . The uptake of electric cars has helped China ramp down oil imports in the wake of the conflict, analysts find .
Emissions from coal, meanwhile, fell by 3 percent, year on year, as the rapid growth of renewables far outstripped the rise in power demand. China added enough wind, solar, and nuclear generation over the same period to power Germany and more than twice as much as needed to meet China’s growing demand. Emissions from the production of steel and concrete also fell amid the ongoing construction slowdown.
China is continuing to build new coal plants despite the decline in coal generation. As the number of generators grows and the use of coal power declines, the average plant is seeing its running hours drop.
The shift from coal to renewables comes even as large volumes of solar and wind power go unused. China is now generating much more clean electricity than its power grid can handle. In the first six months of this year, China rejected roughly a quarter of its wind and solar output.
Analysts say that China lacks the transmission infrastructure necessary to ferry abundant clean energy from where it is generated to where it is needed. Also at issue is a policy that guarantees the purchase of electricity from newly built coal power plants.

articles.title_orig: Salsa Fargo 32 Review: An Intriguing First Move for 32-Inch Gravel
articles.title_zh: Salsa Fargo 32 Review: An Intriguing First Move for 32-Inch Gravel
articles.content_orig:
32-inch wheels offer more stability and better traction than 29-inch wheels
The geometry is well suited to handle the added weight and bulk of bikepacking equipment
Well-made and lightweight metal frame, considering the added dimensions of 32-inch wheels
High front end that makes aggressive riding positions impossible.
Slack head tube that prioritizes stability at the expense of precision.
Long wheelbase that can make the bike feel like it lumbers up to speed.
The Salsa Fargo 32 was the first 32-inch gravel bike to hit the market after it was unveiled at Sea Otter in the spring. The new Fargo is touted as a bikepacking-specific bike, which means it is a longer, slacker design than most gravel bikes.
Those qualities also let Salsa tackle some of the challenges of 32-inch gravel bike design, while avoiding other, thornier geometry problems. Conveniently, that produces a platform that is well suited for bike packing. The slack head tube, long chainstays, and tall front end all offer distinct benefits to going long into unknown terrain. The 32-inch wheels also offer benefits, smoothing over some of the bumps and rough surfaces without adding the complications of a suspension system.
Nevertheless, in our testing, we primarily rode the bike as a straight-up gravel bike. For that use case, we quickly learned just how many pros and cons arise from the new wheel size standard.
What I love about the Fargo 32 is that it exists! This is a bit of a tongue-in-cheek answer, but I mean it genuinely. If we as an industry are going to sort through what to make of 32-inch gravel bikes, we need 32-inch bikes to ride. And to be the first to market with a genuine, mainstream product is a risk, so big kudos to Salsa for that.
In riding the bike, what I noticed straight away more than anything was better traction. Talk about rollover and stability all you want, traction is where the bike had the most tangible improvement over the other bikes in our Field Test . Since we were able to standardize tires across the range of the bikes we were testing, I noticed straight away how differently the tires were handling the mix of dirt, rock, and roots I encountered on the ride. I could really dig into turns and push the bike downhill with confidence. Braking traction stood out in particular as a huge benefit to the bigger wheels.
On paper, the number-one argument for 32-inch bikes is not traction. Roll-over and efficiency over rough terrain are most frequently cited as the biggest upside of 32-inch gravel. In our testing, I was a bit let down at first. It didn’t exactly feel smooth over many of the bumps that I thought it would. Yet, I think my expectations were too high. Thirty-two-inch wheels do not have suspension, after all.
After I got more time riding the Fargo, I found that roll-over benefit to be a bit more nuanced, presenting itself in more subtle ways. We rode a steep uphill trail that was punctuated by a tough rooted step-up three times with three bikes on our first impressions day . After failing the previous two reps, I cleaned the roots with relative ease on the 32-inch bike. The increased stability, increased contact patch, and the better roll-over all worked together to smooth out the roots, allowing me to power over the feature.
That, paired with the bike’s ability to take a few seconds off my downhill time without feeling like I was risking anything, left me with a great first impression of the Fargo, even if it didn’t quite sweep me off my feet as much as I thought it would.
Those roll-over gains were further backed up in the climbing challenge, through a short, technical ascent where I was able to tackle a mix of gradients and surfaces. Despite the bike not being the lightest, nor the snappiest, the Fargo won the challenge. When I pushed uphill, the bike just held speed over things that bogged down every other option except the drop-bar mountain bike. I wasn’t able to be as precise in placing my front wheel; it didn’t matter. The bike would keep rolling.
It never really felt smooth, but that didn’t matter. It got the job done, and it preserved forward momentum better than the rigid 700c bikes, without a doubt.
All of my issues with the Fargo relate to the inability to get into a true gravel bike position. For some, this simply won’t be an issue. Plenty of riders love the upright position that the bike requires. But for me, the front end was too high even though the bike was sized correctly.
The biggest aspect that limits Salsa’s ability to get the front end of the bike lower is the same aspect that has limited many early 32-inch bikes. Compared to 700c gravel bikes, where there are many carbon fork options to build steel or titanium frames around, there haven’t been 32-inch gravel forks to work with. Instead, early 32-inch gravel bikes have used rigid 29-inch mountain bike forks.
Those forks easily fit the bigger 32-inch wheels, but they have a much higher axle-to-crown length than necessary. That excessive axle-to-crown pushes the stack higher, forcing a higher riding position. There is a limit to how short a bike’s head tube can be.
That upright position is difficult in its own right, but with the added length and slack front end, the bike is not aggressive at all. The larger wheels certainly don’t make the frame feel any snappier. The result is the bike feels like it lumbers up to speed and struggles to hold pace on calm or smooth terrain.
From an ease-of-use perspective, the Fargo 32 is fairly traditional. As you can expect from a bike-packing-centered bike, the frame is built to be configured in a few different ways. All the cables and hoses are externally routed. The seatpost has a conventional 27.2mm seatpost with dropper post compatibility. On the front end, the fork is suspension-corrected. Altogether, the bike has been built to be a modular 32-inch bike built for riders to explore 32-inch wheels on their own terms.
One of the trickier aspects of the move to 32-inch gravel bikes is the lack of a solidified standard for thru-axle spacing. The Fargo 32 uses 110mm Boost front spacing and 148mm Boost rear spacing.  That mix-and-match is key to knowing if you are looking for the right wheelset.
The Fargo 32 is a bike that is great for those looking to go far and those chasing unknown terrain. The bike is not made for speed, but certainly comes into its own the longer the ride. Its relaxed geometry makes it easy to handle, even after a long day. The improved traction from the 32-inch tires provides a bigger margin for error when things get rowdy, another benefit for riders taking on long hauls.
More than anything, what the 32-inch wheels provide the Fargo is a wheel system that can handle whatever is thrown at it. Even compared to suspension, which will always be a little bit wonky on pavement, the bigger wheels just make for a bike that can keep its head above water when things get unpredictable. In bikepacking, where even refined routes can get hairy quickly, that extra capacity can be a huge benefit.

articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump has indicated the possibility of a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss ending the war with Iran. Concurrently, China’s special envoy on Middle East affairs has traveled to Tehran to meet with officials of the Islamic Republic.
Trump told reporters he expects to meet with his Chinese and Russian counterparts on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China next week. According to Trump, ending the war with Iran and nuclear disarmament are expected to be among the topics of discussion.
The Wall Street Journal previously reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin was also interested in holding such a summit to discuss peace in Ukraine.
Meanwhile, Zhai Jun, China’s special envoy on Middle East affairs, met with Ali Bagheri Kani, Deputy Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, and Majid Takht-Ravanchi, Deputy Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, in Tehran.
This visit comes one week after Ali Bagheri Kani’s trip to Beijing, where he met with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. The concurrent visit of the Sultan of Oman to China has further fueled speculation regarding potential mediation by Beijing between Tehran and Washington.
China’s Foreign Ministry stated that the objective of these meetings is to review bilateral relations and regional developments in the Middle East.
According to a statement from the ministry, Zhai Jun referenced the widening regional conflict, emphasizing that the use of force is not a solution and that the sovereignty and security of nations must be respected.
The Chinese envoy is scheduled to continue his regional tour with visits to Oman and Saudi Arabia.

articles.title_orig: EXCLUSIVE: Chinese Bag-Maker Songmont Enters Footwear
articles.title_zh: EXCLUSIVE: Chinese Bag-Maker Songmont Enters Footwear
articles.content_orig:
LONDON — Songmont, the Chinese brand that has made global headlines for cultural storytelling that resonates with China ‘s middle class, will launch its first footwear collection Wednesday.
Known for accessories that translate the landscapes, architecture and craft traditions of brand founder Fu Song’s hometown, Shanxi province, the brand is extending its offering beyond bags, ready-to-wear and fragrance with a footwear range inspired by the Wotou shoe.
Wotou is a traditional style named for its resemblance to a dome-shaped steamed corn bun popular in northern China . Traditionally handmade and padded with cotton, the model’s soft construction and distinctive raised seam informed Songmont’s contemporary interpretation for its debut footwear range.
The new silhouette launching this week, retailing for 2,680 renminbi, or $400, echoes the original, while piping joins two leather panels to recreate the ridge across the upper. Songmont’s tiger-tooth hardware adds a modern detail. The toe combines a square shape with softened edges, and layered leather forms a stepped heel inspired by Shanxi architecture. The style will come in 2.5cm and 6cm heel heights.
Songmont said it has spent more than a year developing the shoes, with 20-plus rounds of fittings and refinements. A custom last was designed to accommodate a range of foot shapes, and the use of full-grain cowhide uppers, a double-layer construction, sheepskin lining and high-resilience cotton insoles is meant to balance support, softness and breathability.
The brand added that the footwear launch builds on a design language it has developed across its collections. Its Gather bag, for example, recalls camel bags of the ancient Silk Road, while the Song bucket bag takes cues from traditional kite frameworks.
“As long as we choose things we genuinely like, the brand remains consistent. If we always chase trends or pay too much attention to what’s new, we can end up not knowing what we want,” Fu said about the brand’s approach in an earlier interview with WWD in Paris.
Founded in 2013, Songmont has around 20 stores in China and is expanding at a measured pace, with a focus on customer experience. It plans to open its first Hong Kong store in December, adding a new address as the brand continues to grow beyond mainland China.

articles.content_orig:

Nearly a year ago, Waymo updated its self-driving software and issued a recall after numerous reports that its robotaxis were illegally passing school buses that had stopped and deployed flashing red lights. Now, federal safety regulators have opened a new investigation into why that behavior has continued.
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) said in a November 6 filing that a majority of these reported incidents occurred after the company deployed a software update intended to fix the problem.
Reuters was the first to report the filing.
Waymo said last year that a software update was completed for all affected vehicles on November 17, 2025. However, NHTSA said the majority of the incidents occurred after the software update. NHTSA’s Office of Defects Investigation (ODI) has opened a “recall query” to “assess the adequacy of the remedy.”
The ODI opened its initial investigation into Waymo in October 2025 after seeing footage of one of its autonomous vehicles maneuvering around a stopped school bus that had its stop sign extended, lights flashing, and was unloading children in Atlanta. In that incident, a Waymo robotaxi crossed perpendicularly in front of the school bus from its right side. The autonomous vehicle then turned left around the front of the bus before traveling down the street.
Numerous other incidents have been documented in the weeks and months since in Austin, where Waymo also operates a robotaxi service. Austin Independent School District officials reported at least five such incidents at the time, according to a letter filed with NHTSA.
Reached for comment, Waymo stressed the importance of safety to its mission. “We have made significant improvements to vehicle behavior around school buses and have received no citations since March 2026,” a spokesperson told TechCrunch via email. “The Waymo Driver has a clearly demonstrated positive impact on roadway safety. Once received, we’ll work to respond to NHTSA’s query and look forward to continuing our engagement on recall processes for AV software that continues to learn and improve.”
TechCrunch also reached out to Austin Independent School District officials for comment and will update the article if they respond.
This article was updated after publication with Waymo’s statement.

articles.title_orig: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists
articles.title_zh: KFC’s arrival at Italian ski slopes angers food and mountain purists
articles.content_orig:
Fast-food outlets at two prestigious Dolomites resorts are Italy’s first, with legal action threatened
Europe live – latest updates
Skiers on the slopes of two of Italy’s most prestigious resorts will be able to dine from buckets of fried chicken between runs this winter as the US fast-food chain KFC prepares to open outlets, infuriating mountain and food purists while prompting a prominent businessman to threaten legal action.
KFC will open its first high-altitude restaurants on the slopes of Cortina d’Ampezzo and Madonna di Campiglio, in the Dolomites, on 5 December, an initiative the company said was aimed at “surprising people” and “reaching places” where nobody would expect to find it.
The move marks a debut for any fast-food outlet on an Italian ski slope, bringing a menu replete with KFC’s most popular products, from spicy wings and burgers to traditional buckets of fried chicken.
The plans appear to have taken people by surprise, not least Alberico Zardini, a majority shareholder in Faloria Spa, the company that manages the infrastructure on Mount Faloria in Cortina d’Ampezzo, where there is to be a KFC at 2,123 metres.
“The mere idea is disgraceful,” Zardini told Il Messaggero . “It’s absurd and shameful to imagine a fast-food joint in the most beautiful spot in Cortina. Do the people of Cortina not realise what we’re risking here?”
Zardini said he had written to the bosses of Faloria warning that he would pursue legal action unless they put the brakes on KFC’s mountain ambitions.
He said it was “a mad decision”, especially because the outlet would be selling fried chicken inside the Faloria mountain club, where a luxury lodge is due to open on an upper floor. “I am 100% against it and will not just sit back and watch,” he said.
The KFC in Madonna di Campiglio, in south-western Trentino on the opposite side of the Dolomites, will be at 1,700 metres on Piana di Nambino, next door to a swish après-ski club.
The two outlets came under the fast food chain’s “quick service restaurants” product range and were the company’s way of targeting a broader market beyond its loyal Gen Z customers, “from young families to mountain lovers”, said Marzia Farè, the chief marketing officer for KFC Italia.
“We strongly wanted this project because it perfectly represents the way we imagine the evolution of KFC: continuing to surprise, reaching places where no one would expect to find us, and doing so without giving up what makes us unique,” she told brandnews.it .
after newsletter promotion
Needless to say, with the cost of ski passes in Italy increasing each year, the outlets will appeal to those looking for cheap food in otherwise extremely pricey resorts.
But Oscar Farinetti, the founder of Eataly, Italy’s high-end food-store chain, has said the brand “doesn’t belong here at all” – while pointing the blame at customers. “We Italian consumers should be a tad more cultured,” he told Il Sole 24 Ore . “We need to acknowledge our assets – our cuisine made of few ingredients and excellent products. There is a lack of studying one’s own roots – we’re eating fried chicken instead of a nice slice of salami with a glass of fresh wine.”
Luigi Casanova from Mountain Wilderness, an NGO that works to protect mountain environments, told Corriere della Sera : “The era of polenta and luganega sausage is over,” while Paola Demagri, from Trentino’s provincial council, spoke about mountain identity being “sold out to Kentucky chicken”.
Others were more measured in their response. Cristian Ferrari, the president of Società Alpinisti Tridentini, the oldest mountain association in the Trentino area, said: “We have nothing against fried chicken, but are we sure this is the issue we should be most worried about?”

According to CBS News, Nvidia's board announced on Sunday, Nov. 8 an independent investigation of CEO Jensen Huang, supervised by independent directors with outside counsel. CBS, citing the New York Times, reported that U.S. intelligence officials say a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed worked for China's Ministry of State Security, which China calls "groundless speculation." The board said in a statement reported by CNBC: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information."

articles.title_orig: A US Official Just Joined Russia’s Special Forces. He Still Holds Office in Vermont
articles.title_zh: A US Official Just Joined Russia’s Special Forces. He Still Holds Office in Vermont
articles.content_orig:
A US official has joined Akhmat, a notorious Russian military unit linked to Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov. With a history of supporting the Kremlin and political ties stretching from Russia to Iran and North Korea, Christopher Helali has now gone from backing Russia’s war against Ukraine to joining its military ranks.
Russia’s Akhmat special forces announced their newest recruit in October 2026, a man who describes himself as Iranian-American, operating under the callsign “Vermont.” Thousands of miles from Russia’s war in Ukraine, the recruit still holds elected public office in the US.
Helali relocated to Moscow after winning public office in the US in 2024. He has since traveled to Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory and persistently supported Russia’s war.
This war must end, and the only way to end it is to eliminate the root causes and ensure that Russia achieves all its goals in a special military operation.
But how did Christopher Helali, the elected high bailiff of Orange County, Vermont, go from holding public office in the United States to joining the military of a country waging war against Ukraine?
Helali’s decision to join Russia’s military did not come out of nowhere. Long before signing a contract with Moscow, the American politician had developed ties with organizations and political figures in North Korea and Iran.
Helali previously served in the US military and worked as a high school teacher in New Hampshire. In 2020, he unsuccessfully ran for the US House of Representatives as a communist candidate , receiving approximately 1% of the vote.
His political activities have taken him far beyond US borders. He reportedly traveled to Syria to fight alongside Kurdish forces against ISIS.
From June 2024, Helali headed the North American Executive Committee of the North Korean International Solidarity Group, an organization promoting support for Pyongyang. In March 2026, the group reported that Helali met its president, Zheng Yutong, in Beijing, where they discussed activities commemorating former North Korean leader Kim Jong Il and plans to strengthen cooperation with the American Communist Party.
Helali resigned as the party's international secretary in July 2026, during his visit to Iran, where he honored former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei who was killed in US-Israeli strikes earlier that year.
Helali declared that he would “pray for Imam Khamenei and his family.” On X, he repeatedly identified himself as the “ELECTED High Bailiff of Orange County, VT, USA” and claimed to be the only elected American politician in Iran at the time.
Helali was accompanied in Iran by Jackson Hinkle, an American pro-Kremlin influencer known for spreading disinformation about Russia’s war against Ukraine. Both men have visited Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory and participated in a Russian-sponsored briefing at the United Nations, where Hinkle accused Ukraine of terrorism and defended Moscow’s actions.
This is treason. Arrest this scumbag the second he lands back in America. https://t.co/4VPHTRdehi
Following his Vermont election, his activities have mainly centered on Russia and Iran. Helali moved to Moscow in 2025, citing what he described to Vermont reporters as “increased scrutiny and oppression” from the US government and his local community.
Describing himself as an “investigative journalist,” Helali uses social media platforms, including his X account with more than 50,000 followers, to promote Kremlin narratives and openly endorse Russia’s territorial claims over Ukraine. “Crimea IS and ALWAYS will be RUSSIA!” he declared in one post. In another, he insisted, “DONETSK IS AND ALWAYS WILL BE RUSSIA!”
How far back his ties to Moscow go remains unclear. While filming a report for Russian media in the Kursk region, Helali claimed to have supported the Russian cause since 2014. He also participated in a briefing organised by Russia’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations promoting the 2024 World Youth Festival in Sochi, which he later attended.
Helali has echoed these Kremlin talking points, describing his inclusion in Ukraine’s Myrotvorets database following visits to Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory, as an honour and as part of a fight against what he called “Bandera and neo-Nazi ideology.”
In May 2026, Helali joined more than 50 foreign journalists on a Russian-organised visit to Starobilsk in occupied Luhansk, following a strike Moscow claimed had killed college students. Ukraine stated it struck military infrastructure including ammunition depots, air defense systems, and the headquarters of the Rubicon unit. Speaking to Russian state media at the scene, Helali accused Ukraine of deliberately targeting civilians and called for Moscow to achieve its military objectives. Throughout its full-scale invasion, Moscow has repeatedly promoted its account of its invasion through foreign visitors and media personalities.
In June 2026, Russian media reported that Helali had personally written to Vladimir Putin requesting Russian citizenship. Then, his ambitions went beyond a Russian passport. In October 2026, Akhmat commander Apti Alaudinov announced that Helali had completed military training and signed a contract to serve in the unit.
When Russian state media asked when he would deploy to the frontlines, Helali claimed he was already taking part in the “special military operation”—the Kremlin’s propaganda term for its war against Ukraine. What Helali is actually doing within Russia’s military is still unclear.
“I admired their professionalism, brotherhood, discipline and respect for both religions of my family—Orthodox Christianity and Islam,” Helali said in an interview with Russian state media.
Akhmat special forces are linked to Chechen leader Ramzan Kadyrov and commanded by Alaudinov. UNITED24 Media has previously reported allegations of serious human rights abuses involving Akhmat units , including the torture and extrajudicial killing of civilians, looting, and the operation of detention facilities in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territory.
Back in Vermont, the high bailiff’s position is largely ceremonial but carries specific legal responsibilities. Under state law, the high bailiff can serve legal documents that the county sheriff cannot and assume the sheriff’s powers in certain circumstances, including when the office becomes vacant.
UNITED24 Media reached out to the Orange County Sheriff, George Contois, who said that Helali has had no involvement with his office and that his “duty as High Bailiff would be to arrest the Sheriff and I've yet to be arrested…He has done absolutely nothing and has remained anonymous to my office,” Contois said.
Contois added that he was aware of the scrutiny surrounding Helali, but despite Helali’s relocation to Russia and his military enlistment, the sheriff said he has “not heard of any effort to remove him for cause; simply let his term run out,” Contois said, “To my knowledge, he has not sought re-election.” The sheriff also confirmed that he is “yet to see the man, only photos.”
In the November 3, 2026 US midterm elections, Republican J.T. Dodge secured the Orange County High Bailiff seat. Dodge is expected to replace Helali when his term expires in February, 2027. Until then, Helali remains an elected US official.
Vermont election officials have previously confirmed that the position does not require its holder to live in the state, meaning Helali’s move to Russia does not automatically disqualify him from office. But beyond the ethical questions surrounding an elected US official joining the military of a country waging an illegal war against Ukraine, his enlistment raises a more immediate concern: what happens if Orange County actually needs its high bailiff?Under US law, Americans are not automatically prohibited from serving in foreign armed forces, nor does such service necessarily result in the loss of US citizenship. articles.title_orig: Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollution
articles.title_zh: Thick smog shrouds New Delhi after Diwali firecrackers add to seasonal pollution
articles.content_orig:
People walk in front of India Gate, shrouded in thick smog after firecrackers lit up the sky overnight during Diwali celebrations, in New Delhi, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Manish Swarup/AP hide caption
NEW DELHI — A thick blanket of smog shrouded India's capital Monday after firecrackers lit up the skies over New Delhi during Diwali celebrations, compounding dangerously high pollution levels and intensifying the seasonal air pollution crisis that grips the city every year.
Despite restrictions on fireworks, residents in New Delhi celebrated the Hindu festival of lights with firecrackers on Sunday evening, releasing smoke and fine particulate matter into the atmosphere. The air quality index exceeded 350 in several parts of the capital on Monday morning, reaching the severe category and posing significant health risks.
Monitoring stations across the city recorded similarly alarming levels, while visibility deteriorated as a gray haze blanketed streets and high-rise buildings.
India's Supreme Court in October had sought to limit Diwali pollution by restricting conventional firecrackers and allowing only approved "green firecrackers" under specified conditions for three-hour windows on Saturday and Sunday. The crackers produce fewer emissions but are not pollution-free. They still release particulate matter and other pollutants, adding to the city's already hazardous air.
Isyad, a New Delhi resident who uses one name, said the worsening smog was taking a toll on his health.
"Because of the pollution there is irritation in the throat and itching in the eyes," he said.
New Delhi and its metropolitan region, home to more than 30 million people, regularly rank among the world's most polluted areas during winter. Pollution worsens as Diwali fireworks coincide with cooler weather and smoke from crop-residue fires in neighboring states of Punjab and Haryana.
After harvesting rice, farmers often burn leftover stalks to clear their fields for the next planting season. The smoke drifts toward New Delhi, adding to pollution from vehicles, industries, construction dust and other local sources.
The problem becomes particularly acute in late October and November, when cooler temperatures, low wind speeds and stagnant atmospheric conditions prevent pollutants from dispersing. The result is a thick haze that can linger over the capital and surrounding areas for days.
People walk through thick smog after firecrackers lit up the sky overnight during Diwali celebrations in New Delhi, Monday, Nov. 9, 2026. Manish Swarup/AP hide caption
Authorities in New Delhi have implemented a set of measures to curb pollution, which include limits on construction activity and restrictions on diesel generators, while courts have sough restrictions on firecrackers. But the measures have not prevented the return of severe pollution each year.
Environmentalists say long-term solutions, such as cleaner energy and stricter controls on vehicle emissions, are needed to prevent the annual crisis.
Shweta Narayan, a public health expert at the Global Climate and Health Alliance, described the government's response so far as "knee-jerk" and "temporary."
"A lot of interventions happen only because the government is pressured or pushed in a corner to do something," she said.

articles.title_orig: Ukraine Peace Talks Resume This Week in Abu Dhabi
articles.title_zh: Ukraine Peace Talks Resume This Week in Abu Dhabi
articles.content_orig:
A view through the destroyed walls of a kindergarten shows a large bomb crater and a damaged residential apartment building following a missile attack in Kyiv, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. Dan Bashakov/AP hide caption
European officials will turn up for the U.S.-mediated peace talks between Russia and Ukraine in the United Arab Emirates this week, France's foreign minister said Sunday, days after the Kremlin had insisted there could be no role for European powers at the meeting.
"France will be there and will ensure that Europe's voice is heard," Jean-Noël Barrot told French radio. He did not say who would represent Paris, or whether French or other European officials would take part directly in negotiations, or simply observe.
The meetings, which are set to take place in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, had previously been presented as a three-way session between Washington, Moscow and Kyiv.
The Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had earlier ruled out a European role, saying the trilateral format had already been agreed.
Talking to a Russian news channel on Friday, he accused European governments of failing to decide who speaks for them, while acknowledging that security talks would at some point require Europe's involvement.
On Thursday, President Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev and said a coming agreement was "going to involve more than Ukraine," adding he could even say it "might involve all of Europe."
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told CNN on Friday that he had not been given details of the agreement Trump had referenced, and warned: "For me, it's not simple, and it can be dangerous." He invoked the 1945 Yalta conference, where Allied leaders settled Europe's division without the involvement of several affected countries.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, right, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy attend a press conference in Berlin, Germany, Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026. Ebrahim Noroozi/AP hide caption
This will be the fourth round of talks between the two warring nations brokered by the Trump administration, and the first since those in Geneva this February. Earlier U.S.-brokered meetings have made little progress, and the chances of a breakthrough have been reduced as the Trump administration focused on its war with Iran.
Moscow confirmed it would return to the negotiating table only following a visit by U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff to meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg in October. Those talks saw Putin announce the release of an American prisoner from a Russian jail — an apparent Kremlin gesture to President Trump's earlier lifting of sanctions on Russian diesel exports. Ukraine was vehemently opposed to the fuel sales — arguing they helped replenish Moscow's war chest.
Witkoff has said the agenda for these latest talks will include postwar security arrangements and de-escalation of the conflict and humanitarian issues, shortly after Melania Trump helped broker a limited ceasefire that allowed humanitarian aid to enter a town inside Russian-occupied Ukraine.
Russia's delegation will again be led by Vladimir Medinsky, a hardline Putin aide who has participated in most talks with Ukraine since the unsuccessful first set of discussions all the way back in March 2022.
For the first time, these talks will also include Deputy Foreign Ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, as well as Yury Zhigarlovsky, a deputy head of the General Staff's operations directorate, alongside military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov.
This more senior lineup could indicate that Moscow is readier than before to address thorny political and military questions. But the U.S. think tankInstitute for the Study of War suggested some of those same Russian officials have in fact previously sought to slow down previous talks or push harder on Moscow's demands.
The gaps between the two countries remain substantial. Russia has demanded that Ukraine give up large parts of its territory and renounce NATO membership. Zelenskyy has repeatedly insisted any security commitments should be clearly spelled out, including who would act, and how, if Russia attacked again.
Russian President Vladimir Putin, right, interacts with people at the monument to merchant Kuzma Minin and Prince Dmitry Pozharsky, leaders of the struggle against foreign invaders in 1612, in Red Square in Moscow, Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, during National Unity Day celebrations. Yuri Kochetkov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin hide caption
Some analysts expect little. In an op-ed for the Atlantic Council think tank, the former U.S. ambassador to Ukraine John Herbst argued that Putin had rejected every U.S. proposal Kyiv accepted and preferred participating in peace talks than pursuing actual peace. "Perhaps the only outcome of the talks," he wrote, "will be to agree to another round."
The meetings in the United Arab Emirates also follow Democrats' midterm victories, which Zelenskyy said could improve Ukraine's chances of more U.S. aid.
Russia, too, may be looking to push for the Trump administration's outlines of a Ukraine deal — before a Democratic-controlled Congress arrives come January.
Also hovering over the talks — the prospect of Trump, Xi, and Putin gathering for a trilateral meeting at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China later this month. While details remain murky, all sides have confirmed discussions are underway.
And as officials travel to Abu Dhabi to talk peace, the war has raged on regardless.
Zelenskyy said Russia fired 36 ballistic missiles at the Kyiv area overnight Saturday, with only four intercepted, accusing Moscow of treating diplomacy "as a form of aggression."
In southern Ukraine, the death toll from a guided-bomb strike Monday on an aid distribution site in Komyshuvakha rose to at least 55.

articles.title_orig: More than 400,000 Russians killed fighting in Ukraine war, leaked data suggests
articles.title_zh: More than 400,000 Russians killed fighting in Ukraine war, leaked data suggests
articles.content_orig:
Death records reveal losses since full-scale invasion that are unprecedented in Russia’s modern history
Postwar ‘security guarantees’ a key focus in upcoming Abu Dhabi talks, says Rubio
More than 400,000 Russians have been killed fighting in Ukraine since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion nearly five years ago, according to data leaked from the state statistics agency, Rosstat.
The information, obtained by the Belarusian opposition-linked hacker group Cyber Partisans and the Ukrainian hacking collective Silent Crow, contains more than 11m death certificates, including details of the deceased’s age, place of residence and location of death.
It was later shared with the Guardian and a small group of other media outlets.
According to the data, 412,576 death certificates explicitly linked the fatalities to the war, either through official cause-of-death codes or written references to combat and military operations.
The figures underscore the staggering human toll of Russia’s war against Ukraine, with no end in sight despite a fresh round of peace talks scheduled to take place in Abu Dhabi this week.
The two hacking groups announced the breach on 1 November and published the data over the weekend. Rosstat confirmed it had been hacked but denied that any sensitive information had been obtained.
The dataset offers an unprecedentedly detailed picture of Russia’s wartime losses, which Moscow has sought to conceal. The Russian authorities have not published a death toll since the early months of the invasion, and information about military casualties is treated as a state secret.
The Guardian could not independently verify the authenticity of the entire dataset. However, the figures are broadly consistent with other estimates of Russian losses. British intelligence in September estimated that about 500,000 Russian soldiers had been killed since the start of the invasion.
Separately, the independent Russian outlet Mediazona has identified by name nearly 286,000 Russian military personnel killed in Ukraine, drawing on official records, social media obituaries and photographs of gravestones. The outlet estimates the true toll is closer to half a million.
“The data looks authentic, and it’s very rich,” said Janis Kluge, the head of the Russia and Eurasia division at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs.
“This is the biggest leak of data when it comes to Russian casualties,” added Kluge, who has studied Russian war statistics extensively.
The dataset is likely to underestimate the true death toll. Some soldiers remain missing, while others have never been identified.
Kluge also pointed to a significant delay between deaths occurring and being entered into official records, which he said typically took about six months.
“We are probably at this time closer to 500,000 killed Russian soldiers than 400,000,” he said.
The figures also reveal the unequal burden of the war across Russia, with poorer and more remote regions sustaining disproportionately heavy losses.
In Buryatia, Tuva and Zabaykalsky Krai, three regions in eastern Russia, war-related fatalities accounted for about a third of all deaths among men aged 18 to 49 between the start of the invasion and mid-2024. In Moscow and St Petersburg, the equivalent figure was about 10%.
There was also a sharp rise in Russian battlefield deaths as the war dragged on, with some of the deadliest months coming in late 2024 and 2025.
Kluge, who has been analysing the data, said the number of soldiers killed in several months during that period exceeded 15,000, equivalent to roughly 500 a day.
after newsletter promotion
“In late 2024 and in 2025, you see that the numbers in many months are above 15,000 per month, and that’s higher than I think most estimates were,” Kluge said. “That’s 500 a day, above 500 a day. Certainly shocking.”
The scale of the losses is staggering by any measure and unprecedented in Russia’s modern history.
In less than five years, Russian military deaths in Ukraine are estimated to have exceeded the combined death toll from all Soviet and Russian wars between the end of the second world war and the start of the full-scale invasion more than eightfold. The figure also exceeds the number of US military personnel who died during the second world war.
Rather than push Moscow towards a settlement, the scale of the losses is likely to harden Vladimir Putin’s resolve, according to a person familiar with the Russian president’s thinking.
“Putin understands these numbers, and for him to now settle for anything less than everything he wants would feel like a betrayal of himself and the people,” the person said.
Senior Russian and Ukrainian negotiators are due to meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for the first US-brokered peace talks between them in nine months.
Previous negotiations have made little progress towards ending the war, with Moscow demanding that Ukraine withdraw from the parts of the Donbas region it still controls.
Neither Putin nor his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, will attend the talks. Instead, both countries will send senior delegations, with Donald Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner also expected to take part.
In a post on X, Witkoff said the negotiations would focus on “post-war security arrangement, de-escalation” and humanitarian issues.
European governments have expressed concern that the talks could extend beyond Ukraine to broader questions of European security, including Moscow’s longstanding demands for a reduction of Nato’s military presence in countries bordering Russia.
France’s foreign minister said Paris would participate in the negotiations but the Kremlin subsequently denied that France would be represented.

articles.title_orig: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
articles.title_zh: Birds return to waterfowl park after oil vandalism
articles.content_orig:
Resident birds have returned to Broughshane Waterfowl Park after an oil spill which caused the death of 13 of the flock.
The popular attraction in County Antrim was forced to close after a nearby home heating oil tank was vandalised , causing the oil spill into the pond.
In a post on social media, The Waterfowl Pond confirmed that work is still underway to address the oil contamination and that a number of pens remain out of bounds.
More than 20 birds were transported to the USPCA's headquarters for urgent specialist care following the incident.
The park, which was home to 120 birds, has since reopened.
Broughshane Environment Wildfowl and Wildlife Trust's chairman, Gary Hayward, said about 10-12 birds have returned including two black swans and Nenes.
Hayward said they are back safely in their pens and they are lucky to be healthy.
The Northern Ireland Environment Agency (NIEA) was first alerted to the incident on Thursday 22 October and have been involved in removing the oil waste.
The agency said the substance involved had been identified as home heating oil or kerosene.
Police said about 44 gallons (200 litres) of oil had leaked from the tank which had been damaged at a business premise in the Main Street area of Broughshane.
Hayward said that there is very little evidence of the oil left as the NIEA have removed the majority of it.
"They have made problems a lot less than they could have been," he told BBC News NI.
He said there is still some oil around the edges, and once the oil leaves the pens the birds will be moved back into them.
The USPCA has also been a key part of the rescue operation.
They said that all of the birds, including geese, ducks and swans, needed bathed and treated due to the level of contamination they suffered.
Unfortunately some had already ingested too much and died as a result.
The Waterfowl Pond offered thanks to the USPCA for looking after the birds.
"We are truly grateful for everything you have done."
It also paid tribute to the support received from the public.
"It's another positive step forward for our park, and we couldn't have got here without you."
Police have said that enquiries into the incident are ongoing and have appealed to anyone with information to come forward.

articles.title_orig: The ‘Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’ Remake Sets An All-Time Metacritic Score Record
articles.title_zh: The ‘Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’ Remake Sets An All-Time Metacritic Score Record
articles.content_orig:
This year in video games, I’ve swung a digital sword more times than I can count. Thrilling action games like Onimusha: Way of the Sword and Phantom Blade Zero have gotten the feel of a sword fight down to a science, as steel clashes and sparks fly in spectacular fashion. But my favorite duels of the year aren’t in any of this year’s most razor-sharp action games; they’re all in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time .
The Switch 2 remake builds on the combat of Link’s 1998 adventure in careful but effective fashion. The Master Sword feels more powerful than ever thanks to killer sound design and a bit of visual pizazz on impact. What the remake doesn’t do, however, is change Link’s moves to give him the most widely used trick in modern action games: the parry. There’s no deflection to be found in Ocarina of Time ’s remake, and that makes a seemingly simple combat system stand out in an unexpectedly refreshing way.
Compared to many modern games, Ocarina of Time ’s swordplay doesn’t require much mastery from players. Aside from a charged spin attack and a leaping slash, Link’s offensive options are limited. Lock on, swing the sword, hit the enemy, and that’s basically all you need to know. Sure, you can block attacks with your shield or use one of your items to switch it up, but you’re always going to follow the same motions to take out a Deku Baba with consistent strikes.
One of my questions heading into the remake was about how much Nintendo would modernize that approach. After all, lots of remakes and remasters these days make reworked combat a priority; just this year, we’ve seen that in projects like The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered and Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced . Rather than following that wave, Nintendo chose to keep Link’s offense relatively unchanged. That can take some getting used to if you play a lot of modern action games that all seem to have some version of a parry, or at least some kind of counterattack.
The quicker you acclimate to Ocarina of Time ’s throwback action, though, the quicker you’ll come to appreciate its elegance. Fights aren’t meant to be long duels against evenly-matched opponents; Link is a master of his craft and can dispatch virtually any enemy in a few hits. Precision and timing are key as you patiently wait for your opening before lunging forward with a strike. The same goes for Link’s evasive maneuvers, which allow him to sidestep and backflip away from incoming attacks. It only takes a few Stalfos encounters to learn their attacks and lock down the right dodge and attack follow-up timing to take one out quickly.
In my review, I compared that to the experience of playing Punch-Out!! . The classic NES game’s staying power comes from the fact that every fight hinges on you learning each enemy’s tells and reacting to them accordingly. Every boxing match is a dance, and you have to learn your half of it. Ocarina of Time functions the same way, pushing you to hit all your marks rather than rush through a careful fight.
There are several fights in Ocarina of Time that test your ability to follow that flow, especially the late-game Iron Knuckles who hit like a truck if you fail to dodge their attacks. The best skill check, though, comes during a clash with Dark Link in the Water Temple. It’s the one time where you find yourself up against a fighter who is as efficient and precise as you, because it is you. Patience is your greatest skill in a battle that will taunt you for swinging wildly while your shadowy foe seemingly has an answer to every mistake you make. It plays out like a theatrically staged fencing match. Once you feel that, every other fight clicks into place, too.
Though it may sound a little simple, Nintendo finds the right way to make every slash feel powerful. Every sword hit is accompanied by an impactful thwack and an explosion of colorful particles. Even slashing the weakest enemies as Young Link feels spectacular, as if your blade has busted them open like a pinata. Those small touches make every hit feel important and satisfying to execute, rather than futile hits against a sponge. I can’t say the same for something like GameFreak’s summer not-quite-a-Soulslike Beast of Reincarnation , where bosses fall to death by a thousand cuts.
It may sound strange to call a combat system rooted in 1998 design fresh, but it really is in a world where so many action games I play feel like variations on a theme. Ocarina of Time may not impress modern players who look for expression in their combat, but you won’t hear anyone labeling it a Soulslike or dubbing it “parryslop.” The battles have an unmistakable texture to them, born out of a focused design philosophy that suits an equally focused swordsman. Who needs a parry when no blade can cross you?

articles.title_orig: Leaker Envisions a Shorter iPhone With a New iOS Layout
articles.title_zh: Leaker Envisions a Shorter iPhone With a New iOS Layout
articles.content_orig:
A future iPhone could keep its current width while becoming shorter, with iOS preserving room for content by moving some controls into the status bar, in a theory shared by the Weibo leaker known as " Instant Digital ."
Instant Digital imagines Apple shortening a non-folding iPhone once its display has only a single camera cutout or the front-facing camera moves entirely beneath the screen. Taking roughly a status bar's worth of height off the display would bring its aspect ratio from around 19.5:9 to closer to 18:9, apparently making the phone easier to hold and use with one hand.
Controls that currently sit below the status bar could share a row with the time and system indicators. Instant Digital's idea is that combining the two rows would let the shorter display show the same amount of information. The leaker described the layout and proportions as personal speculation.
Apple has already changed how iOS uses the space at the top of the screen with the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo . The ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌'s smaller Dynamic Island supports up to three simultaneous Live Activities, up from two on earlier models. On the ‌iPhone Duo‌, iOS fits a compact status bar into the corner and positions the Dynamic Island vertically along the side of the outer display.
The timing of a cutout-free display on the iPhone remains uncertain. The leaker "Digital Chat Station" has said Apple is testing under-display camera technology and has described an intermediate design  with a visible hole for the front-facing camera, similar to the ‌iPhone Duo‌.
In a follow-up post on Weibo , another user said they expect iPhones to retain a camera cutout and a 19.5:9 aspect ratio in both 2027 and 2028. Instant Digital replied that some sources say the cutout could disappear in 2028. Display analyst Ross Young has separately said he expects the 2028 iPhone Pro models to retain a centered camera cutout.
In a separate post , Instant Digital said they had a growing hunch that iOS would change substantially after the 20th-anniversary iPhone launches in 2027. They expect changes to how users interact with the software as well as how it looks.
Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman reported that the anniversary iPhone will have curved glass and thinner bezels in the biggest overhaul to the Pro line since the iPhone X. Digital Chat Station has also said Apple was testing a roughly 7-inch display for the largest anniversary model with the same aspect ratio as the iPhone 17 Pro Max.
The iPhone X offers a precedent for a hardware redesign changing how people use iOS. When Apple removed the Home button in 2017, iOS 11 introduced swipe-up navigation on the iPhone X.

articles.title_orig: Rocket Lab Earnings Loom: Here’s What Investors Need to Know
articles.title_zh: Rocket Lab Earnings Loom: Here’s What Investors Need to Know
articles.content_orig:
@Africa images via Canva, @sickmoose via Canva
Rocket Lab ( RKLB ) jumped 15.4% on Friday to $53. That bounce comes after a rough stretch: the stock is still 30% lower over three months and 65% below its 52-week high of $151.
The damage mostly traces to October 15 , when Rocket Lab pushed NeutroPn’s first launch into 2027 . The medium-lift rocket is the company’s bet on the bigger launch market.
Competitors aren’t waiting. Firefly Aerospace ( FLY ) just signed a $1.3 billion deal to supply engines for AST SpaceMobile’s new Blacklift rocket.
The leader in the field is pulling further ahead too. SpaceX ( SPCX ) posted strong third-quarter results in October, and listed space stocks rallied on the news.
Rocket Lab reports on Monday.
Rocket Lab found air pockets in the carbon-fiber layers of a first-stage propellant tank dome. That pushed the debut out of the fourth quarter.
Analysts now expect a first flight around the second quarter of 2027, and the first paying mission closer to year-end. Management has said adjusted EBITDA should turn positive the quarter after Neutron’s first successful flight.
Revenue has kept compounding through the delays…
The top line is in good shape. The question for Monday is what the delay does to costs.
TIKR tracks 21 analysts on Rocket Lab. How many say “Buy”?
See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Rocket Lab, along with Wall Street’s revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Rocket Lab’s Analyst Ratings
Spacecraft and components do most of the work today. Space Systems made up 81% of second-quarter revenue of $234.1 million.
Contracts keep coming in, too. A record $266 million Space Force missile defense deal arrived in July, and Kepler Communications signed on for Neutron launches in August.
Still, Firefly’s single $1.3 billion engine deal is nearly five times the size of Rocket Lab’s biggest military award.
Backlog sits at $2.36 billion, so revenue visibility is strong. Turning that backlog into profit depends on Neutron.
At 26.3x forward sales, Rocket Lab is priced as a future launch giant. Its trailing operating margin is negative 27.6%, and gross margin is 37.3%.
The balance sheet buys time. Rocket Lab holds about $2.25 billion more cash than debt.
Insider selling won’t help the mood. CFO Adam Spice sold $9.9 million of stock in early October and another $7.4 million this month.
My take: The core business is growing fast and the contract book is real. But this valuation assumes Neutron flies and wins share against SpaceX and a newly funded Firefly, and the delay pushes that test out by at least six months. The average Street target near $102 implies 92% upside, which looks generous until Neutron is on the pad.
Monday’s report is the checkpoint. Watch the EBITDA loss against guidance and any firm Neutron date for 2027.

articles.title_orig: Eli Lilly’s Foundayo obesity pill eases sleep apnea in late-stage trial, paving way for approval
articles.title_zh: Eli Lilly’s Foundayo obesity pill eases sleep apnea in late-stage trial, paving way for approval
articles.content_orig:
Eli Lilly on Monday said its obesity pill Foundayo significantly reduced the severity of obstructive sleep apnea, the most common sleep-related breathing disorder, in patients with obesity, in a late-stage trial.
The drugmaker plans to file by the end of the year for U.S. approval of the daily pill for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, or OSA, in adults with obesity or who are overweight. The results make the pill — which rolled out in the U.S. in April — one of several GLP-1 treatments to show promise in treating the condition.
OSA refers to interrupted breathing during sleep due to narrowed or blocked airways, which can cause drops in oxygen and increases in blood pressure that are associated with serious complications, such as hypertension, heart failure and stroke. The condition affects nearly 1 billion adults globally, including 80 million people ages 20 and over in the U.S., according to the National Council on Aging. Most have never been diagnosed, Lilly said in a release.
Lilly's blockbuster weight loss injection Zepbound became the first medication to win U.S. approval for OSA in December 2024. Patients have limited treatment options outside of that drug and many use cumbersome machines that provide positive airway pressure, or PAP, to allow for normal breathing.
"Foundayo is already making a difference for people living with obesity, and with plans to submit these results to the FDA by the end of the year, we could have the opportunity to help people living with OSA," Dr. Thomas Seck, senior vice president of product development of Lilly Cardiometabolic Health, said in a release.
The trial tested Foundayo in two independent studies, the first of which included 363 patients who were unable or unwilling to use PAP therapy. The second study included 349 people who were on PAP therapy for at least three months at the time of screening and continued that treatment during the trial.
Patients in both studies who took Foundayo started at a low dose and increased it gradually at four-week intervals to different maximum dosages.
Researchers specifically examined how much the pill reduced the so-called apnea-hypopnea index , or AHI, which records the number of times per hour a person's breathing shows a restricted or completely blocked airway. The index is used to evaluate the severity of obstructive sleep apnea and the effectiveness of treatments for the condition.
People who took Foundayo and were not using PAP therapy had an average of 21.1 fewer AHI events per hour at 52 weeks, compared with an average reduction of 4.8 per hour for the placebo, according to the results.
Foundayo also met the trial's second goal in that group, leading to an overall AHI reduction of 43.8% compared with a decrease of 6.3% for the placebo. Lilly said 31.5% of the participants in the Foundayo group met the criteria for remission or improvement to mild OSA.
Meanwhile, patients who were on both Foundayo and PAP therapy had an average of 18.3 fewer AHI events per hour at 52 weeks, compared with an average reduction of 5.5 per hour for the placebo.
Foundayo led to an overall AHI reduction of around 27.5% in that group, compared with a decrease of 3% for the placebo. The company said 19.6% of the participants on Foundayo and PAP therapy also met the criteria for remission or mild OSA.
Foundayo also reduced what's known as the sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden — a measure of how deeply and for how long oxygen levels fall during sleep. That metric fell by 55.9% in people not using PAP therapy and 45.8% in those using it.
Lilly said the pill also helped patients lose roughly 11% of their weight across groups at 52 weeks and helped to lower a marker of inflammation.
The company said the safety data and how well patients tolerated Foundayo were generally consistent with previous trials on the pill.
Around 12% of people on Foundayo who were not using PAP therapy discontinued due to side effects, compared to 3.8% with the placebo. Meanwhile, 6.8% of those on both Lilly's pill and PAP discontinued the drug due to side effects, compared with 0.6% in the placebo group.
The most common side effects were gastrointestinal, including nausea, diarrhea, constipation and vomiting, and were generally mild to moderate in severity. That's consistent with other GLP-1 medications.

articles.title_orig: 'The Best RPG I've Played This Year' - Queen's Domain Is A Low-Key GOTY Contender On Xbox
articles.title_zh: 'The Best RPG I've Played This Year' - Queen's Domain Is A Low-Key GOTY Contender On Xbox
articles.content_orig:
Way back in the mid-'90s, a business software developer called FromSoftware decided to take a crack at making video games and produced a first-person action fantasy game called King’s Field for the original PlayStation. It did well enough to warrant some sequels, and the studio eventually decided to produce a sort of spiritual successor called Demon’s Souls , a major contributor in solidifying what would come to be known as the Soulslike genre.
There are still lots of fans of that original King’s Field gameplay loop that pine for a return to the roots, and while FromSoft has now moved on to bigger things, the indie scene has stepped up in a major way to deliver us a proper successor. Freshly Baked Games' Queen's Domain is a retro-fantasy action RPG that masterfully blends tough combat, addictive exploration, and a thrilling sense of mystery to make this a serious contender for the sleeper hit of the year.
The narrative is set in the Kingdom of Bamaen, a once-peaceful place on the brink of destruction after the resurrection of the evil witch Queen Siraatsu. In an attempt to put an end to the calamity, King Abraon and a group of his strongest warriors sailed to the Isle of Neasied to slay the waking queen before she could regain her full strength, but they never returned and the growing onslaught of monsters seems to indicate they failed. You then take on the role of Prince Berium, who shipwrecks upon the isle and sets out in the hopes of uncovering what happened to his father and putting an end to the threat.
After the initial premise is set up, storytelling then takes a backseat and becomes more of a set dressing that you happen to encounter every now and then. Item descriptions and environmental storytelling help to fill in gaps and give more context, but there are precious few moments where cutscenes or major plot beats play out. This approach works well for the kind of atmosphere that Queen’s Domain has in spades—there’s a menacing, haunting aura hanging over the world as you plumb further into its depths, a lot of which comes from the fear of the unknown.
Gameplay could be most closely described as a slower, first-person Soulslike, tasking you with exploring an interconnected, mazelike world riddled with enemies ready to gank you at every turn. You’ll die a lot, but you’ll also learn a lot along the way, and that learning paired with the incremental upgrades that come with combat and exploration leads to a remarkably satisfying ascending power curve.
Queen’s Domain is the kind of game that feels a lot more intimidating up front than it turns out to be and, as with FromSoft's work, it’s that gradual conquest and mastery of its deeper secrets and mechanics that makes it such an excellent and enjoyable experience.
Combat involves a very methodical pace that prioritises careful, strategic moves during the many tense encounters. Especially at first, a few hits can be enough to put you right at death's door, and healing resources are scarce enough that you'll be stuck with most injuries until you make it to the next shrine. The stakes are pretty high, too, given that death has a terrible finality to it. There are no corpse runs here to offer a chance at redemption—if you die, the game simply sends you back to the last time that you saved and erases all progress since.
You can't just hack 'n' slash your way through hordes of foes, and getting jumped by just three at once can sometimes feel like a notable challenge. When hitting back, a small stamina bar represents your total damage output, and taking a swing empties it completely . You then either have to wait for it to refill if you want another full power attack, or you can get in another shot earlier with proportionately weaker strength.
If you want to double down, you can also hold the attack button to ready a charge move that will do increased damage, but this makes the wait even longer and locks you out of other movement and attack options as you helplessly sit there with your weapon raised.
It may sound frustrating, but this leads to richly rewarding combat encounters once you figure out the nuances of your kit. Every weapon has a different range and its own little quirks to get used to. An early favourite of mine was a short-range torch that can be used to rapidly deal passive fire damage and has a limited-use ranged attack that lets you toss a fireball. The more you use a weapon, the more you’ll level it up and increase its damage output, and some weapons evolve into something more advanced if you use them enough.
You’re constantly finding new additions to your kit that fill in interesting niches, and while you can only carry a few of them on you as active weapons, you’re usually pushed to change up your loadout as you move into new areas and come across new enemy types with different weaknesses and damage type resistances.
This gives you lots of opportunities to familiarise yourself with each weapon’s nuances, building lots of muscle memory and mechanical knowledge alongside the raw stat bumps that make enemies drop faster with each increase.
Despite how central combat is to the loop, it feels like you spend even more time simply exploring the world and trying to tease out the correct path forward. Exploration captures that same sense of awe that some of the early Zelda games instilled, as you find yourself cautiously crawling through a dungeon looking for a key to a door you found or trying to figure out what that switch you just triggered unlocked. There’s no map and few signposts pointing you in the right direction, so a lot of your knowledge of a space comes from stumbling around a new area and trying things.
I was pleasantly surprised to find some Metroidvania elements present to add rewards that keep exploration from getting dull. New abilities, such as an air dash or a throwable knife, give you access to previously gated areas, and you’ll sometimes stumble across a consumable item that permanently boosts one of your stats. This goes a long way in keeping a strong and satisfying sense of forward progression, as you can hardly travel in any direction without finding some upgrade or a new route.
Worth a special mention is just how well Freshly Baked Games champions the themes of wonder and mystery throughout its journey. If you're looking at a distant ledge and wondering if you can get there, the odds are pretty good that you not only can, but there's some sort of treat waiting for you. Sometimes you'll stumble down an obscure side path expecting some minimal pickup, only to suddenly enter an entirely new biome that'll take hours to explore.
The thrill and delight that comes with that constant sense of discovery is something that many modern action games struggle to replicate, and — as much as you can — I would encourage you to go into Queen’s Domain blind and experience everything organically. The magic is somewhat lost if you know where to go and what to do to move forward efficiently, and allowing yourself to struggle with frustrations and overcome them by poking around will be immensely more rewarding.
The graphics are strongly inspired by the blocky aesthetics of the PS1, marked by simplistic environments, chunky models, and unfiltered textures that collectively transcend their lo-fi quality to make for a memorable and fitting art style.
And despite the horror themes present in much of the monster and level designs, there’s a fitting amount of levity to be found in occasional goofiness, such as an unlockable duck-themed shop you gain access to after an early boss encounter. Simple though they may be, the visuals help a lot with immersion, as your imagination fills in the gaps and connects you that much more closely with a given sequence.
The only drawback here is mild performance problems—not present enough to negatively affect the moment-to-moment gameplay, but just enough to be noticeable. In areas with more open space or when you’re being assailed by several foes at once, the fra

articles.title_zh: Germany issues ultimatum to secure Ukraine funding
articles.content_orig:
In brief: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to block the EU’s next seven-year budget unless all member states commit to financing Ukraine in 2027 and beyond, the Financial Times reported. His demand links the bloc’s wider spending negotiations to Kyiv’s urgent funding needs, as several governments resist further contributions and Germany seeks a lasting agreement.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has threatened to block the European Union’s next seven-year budget unless every member state commits to financially supporting Ukraine in 2027 and subsequent years, the Financial Times reported on Monday, Nov. 9.
In a letter to European Council President António Costa, reviewed by the newspaper, Merz made Germany’s support for the bloc’s 2028-2034 budget conditional on a collective commitment to fund Ukraine, the FT reported .

“A collective commitment that all of us, without exception, will contribute fairly to closing [Ukraine’s financing] gap” was essential before further discussions involving financial commitments, Merz wrote.
Ukraine faces an additional financing shortfall of approximately €70 billion ($78 billion) in 2027 as Russia’s continuing war drives up its military and budgetary needs.
Merz also demanded a solution supported by all member states that would provide reliable, multiyear financing from 2028 onward, including interest payments on outstanding Ukraine-related debt.
The warning gives Ukraine’s funding needs a direct place in negotiations over the EU’s wider spending priorities.
The bloc’s long-term budget, formally known as the Multiannual Financial Framework, sets spending limits across policy areas including agriculture, regional development, research and external assistance.
Adopting it requires unanimous agreement among EU governments and the European Parliament’s consent. Germany could therefore prevent approval by withholding its agreement.
The European Commission’s proposal for 2028-2034 envisages mobilizing up to €100 billion ($112 billion) for Ukraine. That remains a proposal subject to negotiations.
The Commission says Ukraine funding would retain flexibility because the country’s needs are large and difficult to predict. Support for operations with military implications would continue through the separate European Peace Facility.
Merz’s demand challenges governments seeking to avoid additional financial commitments while allowing other EU members to proceed.
Hungary, Slovakia, Czechia and Bulgaria have indicated that they would not participate in a new loan for Kyiv, according to reporting on the funding negotiations.
In October, Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico said Slovakia and Hungary would sit out further financing . He also criticized linking assistance for Ukraine to the EU’s future budget.
Germany, the bloc’s largest net budget contributor, is using its negotiating leverage to press for broader participation, the FT reported.
Berlin also wants future Ukraine financing decisions to require a qualified majority rather than unanimity, reducing individual governments’ ability to block subsequent support. That would be a change sought by Germany, rather than an agreed EU arrangement.
The additional €70 billion requirement comes on top of financing already arranged under the EU’s €90 billion ($101 billion) loan covering 2026 and 2027.
EU leaders previously tasked the European Commission with developing options to close the new gap while disbursements continue under the existing package.
Costa has said the EU would normally cover around two-thirds of Ukraine’s additional financial needs, with other partners contributing the remainder. The Commission is examining options, including further joint borrowing.
A final agreement on the financing mechanism has not been reached.
Brussels has also been seeking larger contributions from non-EU partners, including Britain and Canada, as anticipated international support has failed to fully cover Ukraine’s growing requirements.
The effort concerns both sustaining Ukraine’s defense and keeping the state functioning through another year of war. EU officials have emphasized broader international burden-sharing rather than relying increasingly on European taxpayers alone.

articles.title_orig: What Hardware Does Your PC Need To Run A Local AI Model?
articles.title_zh: What Hardware Does Your PC Need To Run A Local AI Model?
articles.content_orig:
I've been a staunch proponent of self-hosting AI for a while now, and the points that I usually make are centered around data privacy and the fiscal cost of self-hosting your own models versus paying for a monthly subscription.
One of the most frequent comments I get says that whatever I save by self-hosting my models is offset by my power bill, which always felt hyperbolic. To find out exactly how much local AI inference adds to my power bill each month, I benchmarked a model with llama-bench, the benchmark tool built into llama.cpp, logged power draw with HWiNFO and Nvidia's own nvidia-smi on my RTX 4070 Ti Super PC, and found that the cost is nowhere close to what I'd pay for a single AI subscription. Here is what I found, and how I measured it.
To make the test and an estimation of cost as comprehensive as possible, I picked Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, which is a model that's too big for my RTX 4070 Ti Super's 16GB of GDDR6X memory on its own, and not lacking in capability at any task I throw at it.
At 16.5GB in its UD-IQ4_XS quantization, I tend to offload the experts from eight of its layers to my Ryzen 5 7600X with llama.cpp's --n-cpu-moe flag to get a comfortable inference speed. This also puts the CPU to work on every token generated by the model, so measuring the GPU alone would have concealed a big part of the power bill, which is exactly why I accounted for the CPU in the cost accounting as well.
I used llama-bench , which is a benchmark test that comes baked into llama.cpp (build b11927) to time the two jobs a model does, which is reading prompts and generating tokens. For this test, I gave the model a 2,048 token prompt to read ten times over and instructed it to generate 512 tokens five times over, both starting from an empty context.
While llama-bench ran, I used HWiNFO to log the CPU's package power and nvidia-smi to log the GPU's board power every half a second. Added together, the two peaked at 237.5W while reading and 251.9W while generating.
Then, I took an approach that can be described as hyperbolic in the accounting of costs, which entailed stacking the deck against myself. I priced every token as if my CPU and GPU drew that peak for the entire run, did not subtract their idle draw, and used the U.S. Energy Information Administration's 2026 projected average U.S. residential rate of 18.2 cents per kWh .
The rest of the system, including the RAM, the fans, and power supply losses wasn't logged by HWiNFO, so I'll show what another 100W on top does, which is the figure I would use as the true "worst case."
Cost per million tokens (USD)
To put that in context, or more aptly, in subscription terms, $20 buys about 110 kWh at the currently projected U.S. average rate. At my measured peak of 251.9W, my PC would have to generate tokens non-stop for roughly 436 hours to burn through that, which works out to about 14.5 hours a day, every day, for a month.
Even with the extra 100W on top, it still comes to around 312 hours, or over 10 hours a day. That's counting generation alone, which is the expensive half of the process, since reading a prompt costs well under a cent per million tokens even if you were to consider the worst case.
At this point, you would've likely realized that comparing the cost of running a local model versus paying for a cloud-based subscription service is quite a ridiculous practice. However, there's one final bit of accounting left, and that's comparing the two.
When you pay for a monthly subscription service, the price of each token remains hidden, but the API rate cards from Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI don't, which makes them the most fitting standard of measure for what a model's output is worth. I compiled their list prices against my measured numbers for a clear comparison.
Input (per million tokens, USD)
Output (per million tokens, USD)
Output vs Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on RTX 4070 Ti S
67x (Introductory pricing)
There are a lot of misconceptions surrounding the cost of running local models on the hardware you own, particularly relating to power draw. Part of what feeds into these misconceptions is the fact that a GPU running close to its rated power looks and feels energy-intensive, so most people assume that a model keeps the GPU pinned to that figure as long as it's running. However, that is rarely ever the case, because token generation leans on memory more than raw compute.
My RTX 4070 Ti Super peaked at 144W while generating and 177W while reading a prompt against its 285W rating, and even with the CPU's draw and an extra 100W on top, I'd have to keep the model generating continuously for over 10 hours a day before it could match one $20 AI subscription.
